description: Event-name aliases, client detection, Cursor stdin normalisation, shared validation and the exact stdout per event per client for the unified hook dispatcher. v2 is authoritative; master values are listed where they differ.

aliases.lookup: exact, case-sensitive dict lookup (_EVENT_ALIASES.get(raw)); unknown name -> main() returns silently without reading stdin
aliases.note: 'stop' is both the camelCase (Cursor) and kebab-case (CLI) spelling of Stop. There is no 'Stop' kebab variant beyond that.

detect_client_rule: explicit flag wins if non-empty and not 'claude-code'; else 'cursor' if cursor_version or cursorVersion is truthy; else explicit or 'claude-code'
normalize_stdin_rules: client != 'cursor': return the same dict unchanged
conversation_id -> session_id (popped) only when session_id is absent
workspace_roots -> cwd = str(workspace_roots[0]) only when cwd is absent and workspace_roots is a non-empty list
if cwd is a str, len >= 3, cwd[0] == '/' and cwd[2] == ':' then cwd = cwd[1].upper() + cwd[2:] (applies to any cwd for cursor)
tool_output -> tool_response (popped) when tool_response absent; elif result_json -> tool_response (popped) when tool_response absent
source defaults to 'startup' when absent (for every event)

validate_common_rules: for session_id, transcript_path, cwd: value = str(data.get(k, '')); if non-empty replace with sanitize_session_id / validate_transcript_path / validate_cwd (see hook_helpers_cases.json). Mutates and returns the same dict. Empty values and missing keys are left as they were.

stdout_rules: SessionStart with a response: json.dump(response) (ensure_ascii=True, separators ', ' and ': ') then '\n'

cli_cases.notes: Dispatcher reads raw bytes and json.loads(bytes) auto-detects UTF-8 (with or without BOM), UTF-16 and UTF-32. The legacy entrypoint reads text stdin; the harness decodes it as strict UTF-8, where a decode error is swallowed by read_stdin -> {}. On real Windows Python 3.13 without UTF-8 mode, text stdin uses the ANSI code page, so the legacy result is locale dependent. serde_json accepts only UTF-8 without BOM.
